case.dek: Carlsbad Technology and HIF Bio dispute whether federal courts must dismiss appeals of remand orders involving supplemental jurisdiction.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests the scope of 28 U.S.C. § 1447(d). This statute generally bars appeals of remand orders. The parties argue over whether this bar applies when a district court declines supplemental jurisdiction over state claims.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 20, lines 13-45

sections.heading: How the case got here
paragraphs: The Supreme Court heard oral argument in this case on February 24, 2009.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 3, lines 7-17

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Carlsbad Technology wants the Supreme Court to allow an appeal of the remand order.
HIF Bio wants the Supreme Court to uphold the bar on appealing the remand order.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Carlsbad Technology argues the statutory bar does not cover discretionary refusals of supplemental jurisdiction.
HIF Bio argues the statutory bar covers all remand orders, including those based on supplemental jurisdiction.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Chief Justice Roberts asked if the rule could limit appeals to unusual situations.
Justice Ginsburg asked why ownership disputes qualify as federal questions rather than state property issues.

paragraphs: This dispute determines whether federal courts can review discretionary remand decisions. It affects the finality of state court proceedings. It shapes the balance between federal and state judicial authority.
